question_text:
Nickel experiences corrosion in an acid solution according to the reaction

$$
\mathrm{Ni}+2 \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}+\mathrm{H}{2}
$$

The rates of both oxidation and reduction half-reactions are controlled by activation polarization.
(a) Compute the rate of oxidation of Ni (in $\mathrm{mol} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}-\mathrm{s}$ ), given the following activation polarization data:

For Nickel

$$
\begin{aligned}
V{\left(\mathrm{Ni} / \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\right)}=-0.25 \mathrm{~V} & V{\left(\mathrm{H}^{+} / \mathrm{H}{2}\right)}=0 \mathrm{~V} \\
i{0}=10^{-8} \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{cm}^{2} & i{0}=6 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{cm}^{2} \\
\beta=+0.12 & \beta=-0.10
\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the rate of oxidation and value of the corrosion potential.

Give your answer as a tuple (the rate of oxidation, the corrosion potential).The units of each required answer are (mol/cm^2s, V), respectively.
response:
This is the classic mixed-potential (activation-polarization) corrosion problem. At the corrosion potential the anodic and cathodic current densities are equal in magnitude, so I set the two Tafel expressions equal:

- Anodic (Ni → Ni²⁺ + 2e⁻): $V_{corr} = -0.25 + 0.12\log_{10}(i_{corr}/10^{-8})$
- Cathodic (2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂): $V_{corr} = 0 - 0.10\log_{10}(i_{corr}/6\times10^{-7})$

Solving gives $i_{corr} \approx 8.80\times10^{-7}\ \text{A/cm}^2$ and $V_{corr}\approx -0.0166\ \text{V}$.

The oxidation rate follows from Faraday's law with $n=2$:
$$r = \frac{i_{corr}}{nF} = \frac{8.80\times10^{-7}}{2(96485)} \approx 4.56\times10^{-12}\ \text{mol/cm}^2\text{-s}$$

The applicable skills (model-validity-range, sigfig-rounding) don't alter the result: the Tafel/activation-polarization model is the stated governing model and is being used inside its valid range, so no model switch is needed. Rounding to the precision of the weakest input (2 sig figs):

$$\boxed{(4.6\times10^{-12},\ -0.017)}$$
